newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ'S SFO chief fails to appear at select committee.
newsitem.headline: NZ'S SFO chief fails to appear at select committee.

text.p: The director of New Zealand's Serious Fraud Office, Charles Sturt, has been temporarily stood down from his job because of ill health, officials said on Thursday.

The State Services Commissioner, in charge of all civil service branches, has asked Charles Sturt to temporarily stand down because of concerns about his health, parliament's Justice and Law Reform select committee was told.
An official from the State Services Commission, David Bradshaw, said he had been called-in to be the acting SFO director while Sturt takes a three week overseas holiday.
Sturt had been scheduled to appear before a select committee today but he failed to appear.
"Charles Sturt is not here for health reasons," Bradshaw told the committee.
State Services Commissioner Don Hunn is investigating whether Sturt misled Parliament over the so-called "Winebox" inquiry into alleged tax fraud.
Sturt's health broke down at one stage last year while giving evidence to inquiry.
